metadata.note: The Baltimore Metro SubwayLink, Maryland's only heavy-rail metro system, operated by the Maryland Transit Administration. Unlike most of this map's content, this line is still running today. It opened in stages: the original 7.6-mile trunk from Charles Center to Reisterstown Plaza opened Nov 21 1983; a 6.1-mile extension northwest to Owings Mills (partly running in the median of I-795) opened Jul 20 1987; and a 1.6-mile extension southeast from Charles Center to Johns Hopkins Hospital opened May 31 1995, completing today's 15.4-mile, 14-station, reverse-J-shaped route. Geometry is a real-station waypoint approximation, straight-line segments between the 14 stations -- NOT digitized from the actual (mostly underground/tunneled) track alignment.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Metro_SubwayLink (opening dates: original Charles Center-Reisterstown Plaza segment Nov 21 1983; Owings Mills extension Jul 20 1987; Johns Hopkins Hospital extension May 31 1995; 14 stations, 15.4 miles total)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact current headways by time of day (weekday peak is roughly 8-10 minutes per MTA schedules, not independently verified here); precise mileage/timing between individual stations, all estimated.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
